end.summary:
Practised total distance, displacement, average speed, and average velocity using out-and-back motion.
Practised acceleration using a = (v − u)/t, including negative acceleration; some calculations were right but not steady yet.
The idea that acceleration can include slowing down was corrected later using a negative acceleration example.
Zero velocity at an instant was still linked to zero acceleration; this needs checking again next time.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the difference between distance/displacement and speed/velocity, then used a = (v − u)/t with positive, negative, and zero changes. Diya’s method for identifying negative acceleration was corrected later in the lesson: they used the change from 12 to 0 and included the minus sign. A remaining mix-up was that zero velocity means zero acceleration; at home, pause a ball’s upward motion at its highest point and discuss whether its velocity and acceleration are both zero.
